BUG REPORT (from a user): "I'm using the random and round-robin load balancers (middleware/proxy.go), and I tried asking one for the next target when the target list was empty. I expected `Next` to return `nil` so my handler could respond with a 'no target available' error, but it panicked instead. With the random balancer I got `panic: invalid argument to Intn`; with the round-robin balancer I got `panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero`.
```
rb := NewRandomBalancer(nil)
rb.Next(c) // panic: invalid argument to Intn

rrb := NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*ProxyTarget{})
rrb.Next(c) // panic: runtime error: integer divide by zero
```"

YOUR JOB: Investigate middleware/proxy.go (and its docs/comments, which are the in-repo contract for expected behavior). Fix the bug so that `Next` returns nil when there are no targets, instead of panicking. Check the documented behavior of the Balancer interface / ProxyTarget and make the code consistent with the repository's own documentation. Keep the change minimal and idiomatic. Make sure `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./middleware/...` passes (all pre-existing tests must still pass). Write a small throwaway Go test in /tmp (NOT in the repo) or a tiny main program to prove that Next returns nil for an empty target list for both balancers, and report the exact evidence.

REPORT BACK: the file(s) and exact diff you made, the evidence that the panic is gone and nil is returned, and the exact `go test` output for ./middleware/... .

BUG REPORT 1 (from a user): "When a request doesn't match any registered route, the context still reports the requested URL as its path, so I can't tell 'no route matched' apart from a real match. I expected the path to be empty in that case, since it's supposed to be the path of the route that was matched.
```
e := echo.New()
e.GET("/users/:id", handler)
e.HTTPErrorHandler = func(err error, c echo.Context) {
    fmt.Println(c.Path()) // requesting /does-not-exist prints "/does-not-exist", I expected ""
}
```
I only see this for unmatched requests; matched ones behave as documented."

BUG REPORT 2 (from a user): "I use Scheme() to build absolute URLs. A proxy in front of my app sometimes sends an X-Forwarded-Proto value that isn't a real scheme, such as ftp, and I also set X-Url-Scheme: https as a fallback. I expected Scheme() to ignore the bogus value and use the valid fallback, or default to http if nothing valid is present. Instead it returned the bogus value, so my links were generated with ftp://.
```
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Proto", "ftp")
c.Request().Header.Set("X-Url-Scheme", "https")
fmt.Println(c.Scheme()) // prints "ftp", expected "https"
```"

YOUR JOB: Investigate context.go (and echo.go / router.go as needed) plus any in-repo documentation/comments that state the expected behavior (e.g. the doc comments on Path() and Scheme(), README, CHANGELOG). Fix both bugs minimally and idiomatically, consistent with the repository's own documented contract. Note that both fixes are likely in context.go, so do them in ONE agent (you) to avoid conflicts. Make sure `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test ./...` passes: all pre-existing tests must still pass. If a pre-existing test conflicts with the fix, report that fact and do NOT break the test.

REPORT BACK: the file(s) and exact diff you made, the exact `go test ./...` output, and any pre-existing test that conflicts with the documented behavior.

BUG REPORT (from a user): "I'm binding query parameters into a map so I can keep every value for keys that appear more than once, but it doesn't work the way I expect. With a `map[string][]string` destination the request panics with a message like `reflect: SetMapIndex: value of type string is not assignable to type []string`, instead of giving me all the values for each key. Binding into a `map[string]interface{}` doesn't panic, but each key ends up holding a single string rather than the slice of values I sent.
```
m := map[string][]string{}
if err := c.Bind(&m); err != nil {
    return err
}
```
For a request like `?tag=a&tag=b` I expected `m` to be `{"tag": ["a", "b"]}`."

YOUR JOB: Investigate /echo/binder.go (DefaultBinder, bindData / bindDataToMap and the map binding path) plus any in-repo documentation or doc comments stating expected behavior (README, CHANGELOG, comments on Binder). Fix the bug minimally and idiomatically so that binding query/form params into a map collects all values for repeated keys: `map[string][]string` must not panic and must receive all values, and `map[string]interface{}` should also hold the slice of values (or at least be consistent with the documented behavior). Read the existing tests in binder_test.go to understand the expected shape of the behavior (do NOT modify tests). If a pre-existing test conflicts with the fix, report it and do NOT break the test.

VERIFY: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./...` must pass (all pre-existing tests green). Also write a throwaway program/test OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/bindcheck) that performs a real HTTP request with `?tag=a&tag=b` through echo and binds into `map[string][]string` and `map[string]interface{}`, showing the resulting map contents. `go` is at /usr/local/go/bin/go (not on default PATH).

REPORT BACK: the file(s) and exact diff you made, the evidence (program output), and the exact `go test ./...` output.

BUG REPORT (from a user): "I'm registering two route groups that share the same path prefix, each with its own middleware, and the routes from the first group stop working as soon as I add the second one.
```
e := echo.New()
g1 := e.Group("/group", m1)
g1.GET("", h)
g2 := e.Group("/group", m2)
g2.GET("/other", h)
```
I expect `GET /group` to run `h` with `m1` and `GET /group/other` to run `h` with `m2`. Instead, `GET /group` comes back as `404 Not Found` even though I registered it, and only the second group's route responds correctly; if I delete the second group, the first one works again."

YOUR JOB: Investigate /echo/echo.go (the Group/Add/AddRoute methods, group middleware handling, and anything that mutates already-registered routes when a new group is created) and /echo/group.go and /echo/router.go. Find the root cause and fix it minimally and idiomatically so that both groups' routes work independently with their own middleware. Do NOT change public API signatures. Read the existing tests (echo_test.go, group_test.go, router_test.go) to understand expected behavior; do NOT modify tests. If a pre-existing test conflicts with the fix, report it and do NOT break the test.

VERIFY: `cd /echo && go build ./... && go test -count=1 ./...` must pass (all pre-existing tests green). Also write a throwaway program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/groupcheck) using a `replace github.com/labstack/echo/v4 => /echo` go.mod that reproduces the exact scenario above with two middlewares m1/m2 that set distinguishable headers, and show with httptest (or a real server) that GET /group returns 200 with m1 applied and GET /group/other returns 200 with m2 applied. `go` is at /usr/local/go/bin/go (not on default PATH).

REPORT BACK: the file(s) and exact diff you made, the root-cause explanation, the evidence (program output), and the exact `go test ./...` output.
